Odin × Godot

Exporting — shipping your game

7 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
How export works (both targets)Native desktop (macOS) — verifiedBox3D supported-desktop orchestrationCross-compile (Linux / Windows) — build-verifiedWeb / WASM — verified in a real browserVerify it headless

The editor export plugin compiles .odin scripts ahead of time and bundles the resulting library into the exported game. Players do not need an Odin compiler. Native desktop and web/WASM exports use different library layouts, described below.

Implementation notes on plugin registration, per-platform bundling, and the when WEB split are in design/export-internals.md and design/web-internals.md.

How export works (both targets)#

Two GDExtension classes in core/export_plugin.odin are registered at editor initialization and are absent from running/exported games:

  • OdinExportPlugin (EditorExportPlugin) builds and bundles scripts. On _export_begin, it reads the target OS from export features and resolves tools in this order: odin_godot/odin_bin / odin_godot/emcc_bin project settings, ODIN/EMCC environment variables, then PATH. Project settings let it find tools when the editor starts outside a toolchain shell. It runs the matching build script and calls add_shared_object to include the compiled library beside the executable.
  • OdinEditorPlugin (EditorPlugin) constructs and registers the export plugin.

Godot exports the core library from the .gdextension manifest's [libraries] entries. The plugin adds the dynamically loaded scripts library, which is not listed there. At runtime, native exports locate scripts beside the core through dladdr; the packed res:// filesystem cannot provide a library to dlopen.

The exporter bundles libodinscripts without collecting its transitive native dependencies. Pure-Odin scripts are self-contained. If scripts use foreign import for a third-party native library, bundle that dependency separately, for example through add_shared_object in a custom export plugin or by placing it beside the executable. A missing dependency causes dlopen to fail on the player's machine, leaving the game without Odin scripts.

Script modules. If the project uses script modules (res://modules/<name>/), the export plugin builds one optimized dll per module and bundles each beside the main scripts library, where the exported game scans for them at runtime. A missing module library fails export with an error naming the module. BUILD_MODULES=0 skips module building and bundling and warns that their classes will be absent. Use it for scoped builds or CI checks, not release exports. On web, all modules link into the single wasm. See Script Modules — Exporting.

Optional Box3D profile. The normal exporter also deploys the profile's verified shared Native library beside Core and the script modules. The authored Kit and Replay samples passed actual exported Host/Client runs on macOS arm64 and translated Linux x86-64. Core discovers the Native API through its stable host service; it need not import the engine directly. Gameplay consumers share one Native image. See Gate C for records, architecture boundaries, memory requirements and unsupported claims. These results do not extend Box3D qualification to Windows or web. The current per-target table, toolchain/format identities and minimum-OS limits are in desktop compatibility; maintainer changes follow the pinned upgrade workflow. Native Linux x86 hardware CI is not inferred from Rosetta execution or workflow source.

Native desktop (macOS) — verified#

The macOS export test verifies that the exported .app loads the extension and runs an Odin script compiled during export.

Shell
$GODOT --headless --path your_project --export-release "macOS" out/Game.app

A verified bundle looks like:

Code
out/Game.app/Contents/MacOS/Game                          (universal template, ad-hoc signed)
out/Game.app/Contents/Resources/Game.pck                  (project + rewritten .gdextension)
out/Game.app/Contents/Frameworks/libodin_godot.dylib      (core — auto-exported by Godot)
out/Game.app/Contents/Frameworks/libodinscripts.dylib     (scripts — bundled by the plugin)

tests/phase5/run.sh reproduces this headless end to end (PHASE5_OK): it builds core, runs a headless --export-release "macOS" export (the plugin compiles and bundles the scripts dll), then runs the exported .app headless and asserts the Odin _ready ran.

For the current authored Box3D samples, macOS arm64 is the preset name; its official launcher selector is universal. Actual SDK Core/scripts/modules and shared Native are ARM64, and only ARM64 execution was validated. The launcher plist minimum11.0 does not apply to the whole bundle: the actual exported SDK/Native consumers declare minos14.0 (SDK14.4); tested host macOS15.8. Do not claim macOS11..13 or Intel support from the launcher alone. These current records use strict logs and do not grant a blanket waiver for older fixture warnings.

macOS export gotchas:

  • The installed macos.zip template ships only a universal binary, so the preset must use binary_format/architecture="universal" (not "arm64"), else "Requested template binary … arm64 not found". It runs fine on arm64.
  • arm64 export needs ETC2 ASTC: rendering/textures/vram_compression/import_etc2_astc=true in project.godot, else export aborts.
  • Two non-fatal Required virtual method … _update_exports / _get_script_signal_list warnings may print during the export's class scan. These are harmless.

Box3D supported-desktop orchestration#

tests/box3d_desktop/run.py accepts explicit --target macos-arm64|linux-x86_64, --framework kit|replay, --godot, --odin, --native-library, --native-sha256, --out (NEW and outside the repository), --port and --ticks 120. Default execution is STAGED_ONLY; --execute reuses the normal Gate C exporter and actual exported-pair controller. Linux also needs an explicit --execution-mode native|translated-linux-x86_64 and --toolchain-report. Plans/configuration, successful export and successful runtime are separate facts. Do not force a project --path or ODIN_SCRIPTS_DLL override to make an exported binary appear runnable. Keep actual artifact/native/domain/source/loader fences. See upgrade.md for a concrete plan command and CI/release qualifications; no remote CI run is claimed by this documentation.

The following generic SDK cross-build section retains its earlier scope; it is not the current Box3D Linux exported-run record and does not qualify Windows.

Cross-compile (Linux / Windows) — build-verified#

odin_godot cross-builds the Linux .so and Windows .dll (core + scripts) from macOS. Odin's own driver refuses to cross-link a dll, so build/build_cross.sh emits a single relocatable object (-build-mode:obj -use-single-module -target:<t>) and links it with a Nix cross gcc wrapper (pkgsCross.gnu64 / pkgsCross.mingwW64) that carries the target glibc / mingw sysroot:

Shell
nix develop .#cross --command bash -c 'bash build/build_cross.sh linux   tests/phase35'
nix develop .#cross --command bash -c 'bash build/build_cross.sh windows tests/phase35'

tests/cross/run.sh checks output format, architecture, and exported entry symbols. It reports SKIP if the cross toolchain is unavailable. These checks verify builds; they do not run Linux/Windows Godot or load the resulting libraries on those targets. See distribution.md for the status table, packaged addon, and target-host runtime checks.

Web / WASM — verified in a real browser#

The core ScriptLanguageExtension, generated binding, and compiled scripts link into one Emscripten SIDE_MODULE wasm bundled by Godot's web exporter. A headless-Chrome test checks that a script's _ready runs in the browser and a @(gd_method) returns the expected value. tests/web_showcase/ also checks the pure-Odin coin-collector game loop in-browser.

Toolchain setup (one-time)#

Web export needs the Odin compiler and Emscripten on the export host. The Nix development shell supplies both. For an addon installed in another project, configure them once:

  1. Install the Emscripten SDK from https://emscripten.org/docs/getting_started/downloads.html:

    Shell
    git clone https://github.com/emscripten-core/emsdk && cd emsdk
./emsdk install 4.0.20 && ./emsdk activate 4.0.20

    Use 4.0.20 to match the dylink/longjmp ABI of Godot 4.7's web templates. The Web caveats below describe verification with another emcc version.

  2. Point the editor at the binaries. When you launch Godot from Finder/Steam/the Project Manager, the editor process doesn't inherit your shell PATH, so it can't see odin or emcc. Set these project settings to their absolute paths (Project → Project Settings, "Add" a custom property):

    • odin_godot/odin_bin → your odin
    • odin_godot/emcc_bin → …/emsdk/upstream/emscripten/emcc

    The export plugin uses these settings to find tools, build the wasm, and bundle it from the export dialog. Alternatively, launch the editor from a terminal where both are already on PATH (e.g. after source ./emsdk/emsdk_env.sh).

Build the wasm#

Shell
bash build/build_web.sh your_project
# -> your_project/bin/libodin_godot.wasm  (one Emscripten SIDE_MODULE)

Native builds load scripts separately through dlopen. Web builds link the core, binding, and scripts ahead of time into one side module. The build switch -define:ODIN_GODOT_WEB=true and architecture-gated files select this in-module path, excluding dlopen, hot reload, and editor/export code.

Export and serve#

Shell
$GODOT --headless --path your_project --export-release "Web" out/index.html

The example projects configure these requirements:

  • The project .gdextension keeps its native macos.* entries and adds web.{debug,release}.wasm32 = "res://bin/libodin_godot.wasm". The native entry is what loads the extension on the macOS export host so the loader recognizes your .odin files and packs them into the .pck. Without it, the sources are excluded and base types can't resolve in the browser.
  • The Web export preset needs variant/extensions_support=true (selects Godot's dlink web runtime).
  • The editor's export plugin runs build/build_web.sh at export time to produce the wasm file referenced by .gdextension.
  • Script code must not import core:os, because Odin's native OS layer does not compile for wasm. Importing it produces errors in core/os files, such as Undeclared name: _read_directory_iterator. Use engine APIs instead: gd.singleton_os() + gd.os_get_environment(...) / gd.os_has_environment(...) work on every platform (see examples/barrage/scripts/game_state.odin for the pattern).
  • Odin's int is 32-bit on wasm32 (it's pointer-sized). Never store an engine 64-bit value, especially instance IDs from object_get_instance_id, in int. The code can compile and work natively while truncating IDs on web, causing gd_instance_from_id to return no object. Use i64/gd.Int for IDs and anything else that is 64-bit engine-side.

Serving: Godot web needs SharedArrayBuffer, which requires two HTTP headers:

Code
Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy:   same-origin
Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp

Configure these headers on the serving host. python -m http.server does not set them by default. The addon includes a Node server that supplies them:

Shell
bash addons/odin_godot/build/serve.sh path/to/export_dir   # then open http://localhost:8099/

Use the same two headers in deployment. On itch.io, enable "SharedArrayBuffer support" in the HTML5 settings to configure them.

Web caveats#

  • The browser offers no hot reload (there is no dlopen, and only one shared linear memory is used with the engine).
  • Native debugging isn't available: debug with gd.print, which prints to the JS console and browser devtools.
  • Emscripten version: Godot 4.7.1's web templates were built with emscripten 4.0.20; the module runs with the dev shell's 5.0.6 too (-sSUPPORT_LONGJMP=wasm keeps the longjmp ABI self-contained and the dylink format is cross-compatible). To pin the exact version anyway: EMCC=/path/to/emsdk/.../emcc bash build/build_web.sh.

Verify it headless#

Shell
nix develop --command bash -c 'bash tests/phase5/run.sh'        # native -> PHASE5_OK
nix develop --command bash -c 'bash tests/web/run.sh'           # web    -> PHASEWEB_OK
nix develop --command bash -c 'bash tests/web_showcase/run.sh'  # web game loop -> PHASEWEBSHOWCASE_OK

The web tests are browser-gated: with Chrome + puppeteer-core present they run in a headless browser and assert the Odin script ran; without them they still build + web-export and report a non-fatal SKIP. The full suite (tests/run_all.sh) wires all of these in.
